title: Unified audit envelope + delta protocol for SSO & RBAC v2 events
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a single, extensible audit event envelope and a compact delta (diff) protocol optimized for: RBAC v2 configuration changes, SSO/SAML provisioning events, and admin console actions. Goals are: backward compatibility with existing storage schemas, robust actor/target semantics that map to RBAC v2 principals, compact transmission for high-throughput systems, and explicit rules for redaction and sampling.

Motivation and scope:
- Existing audit artifacts partially overlap (event shapes, actor/target typing, and diff encodings) and lead to inconsistent consumer behavior across Console, Dedicated, and Private control planes.
- New RBAC v2 introduces fine-grained permission objects (principal -> resource -> permission tuple). We must log configuration changes at a granularity that allows: historical permission reconstruction, forensic queries (who granted X to Y), and automated regressions detection.
- SSO/SAML provisioning (assertions, SCIM sync, identity provider config changes) produce noisy, but important, events that need normalization so downstream security tooling can reliably alert on identity drift.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Unified envelope (stringified example below)
- schema_version: semantic version string for event contract (e.g., "1.0.0")
- event_id: globally unique id (UUIDv4)
- occurred_at: RFC3339 timestamp with timezone
- event_type: namespaced type (e.g., "rbac.v2.policy.change", "idp.saml.config_update", "admin.console.login_failure")
- actor: normalized principal object reference (see actor rules)
- target: list of typed resources affected (see target rules)
- outcome: enum (success | failure | partial)
- delta: optional compact diff payload (see delta protocol)
- evidence: optional list of artifacts (links to PRs, audit snapshots, SCIM reports)
- meta: freeform key/value strings for routing (tenant_id, region, release)

2) Actor rules:
- All actors must be normalized to one of: human_user, service_account, external_idp (SAML/OAuth), system.
- Required actor fields: id (opaque stable identifier), type (one of above), display_name, origin (if external: idp name), principal_scope (tenant org id or global).
- For actions initiated via SSO but proxied by a service (e.g., SCIM sync), record both initiator and effective_actor. Use actor.effective_id and actor.initiator_id fields in the envelope.

3) Target rules:
- target is a list of objects with required fields: type (e.g., "role", "permission", "service", "resource"), id, display_name, parent_id (optional), and resource_fingerprint (hash for change detection).
- For RBAC v2 policy changes, include a canonicalized permission tuple string: "principal:<principal_id>|resource:<resource_id>|perm:<perm_name>" in target.external_refs.

4) Delta (diff) protocol (compact and verifiable):
- delta.type: one of (json-patch, kv-diff, op-log). For RBAC-heavy changes prefer kv-diff for compactness.
- kv-diff encoding: a list of entries: [<path>, <op>, <old_value_fingerprint>, <new_value_fingerprint>]. Example: ["/roles/role-123/permissions/0","remove","sha256:abcd","sha256:null"].
- When full payloads are required (for replayability), delta MUST reference a snapshot id stored in the immutable audit snapshot store rather than embedding large objects.
- All diff entries must include canonical path normalization rules (ordered keys, stable array ordering by id) to ensure deterministic fingerprints.

5) Redaction & PII rules:
- PII fields are enumerated in a central policy (confluence://security/pii-policy). The envelope must support two orthogonal transformations: redaction and tokenization.
- Redacted fields are replaced with stable tokens like "[REDACTED:PII_HASH:sha256:... ]" so analytics can still link related events without exposing raw values.
- Sampling decisions MUST be recorded in meta.audit_sampling.reason and meta.audit_sampling.rate for downstream consumers.

6) Retention, storage and backward compatibility:
- Events with delta.type=kv-diff are targeted for hot-store indexing for 90 days, with snapshots retained 365 days by default (configurable per-tenant).
- schema_version bumping policy: backward-compatible additive changes allowed in minor bumps. Breaking changes require migration path (dual-writing old and new envelope for a minimum of 90 days).

7) Integrations and usage patterns:
- Console: use unified envelope for all admin actions (policy edits, user invites, SSO config toggles) so UI timelines can reconstruct causality.
- RBAC v2 engine: on policy evaluation change, emit both an "rbac.v2.policy.change" and a derived "rbac.v2.eval-impact" event that includes a compact list of affected principals for immediate alerting.
- SSO/SAML: normalize idp metadata changes to "idp.saml.config_update" and SCIM sync diffs to "idp.scim.provisioning.delta".

8) Querying and dashboards:
- Provide example Kibana/Datadog queries to answer: who granted permission X in last 30 days; list of failed SAML assertions by idp; top 10 service accounts making admin changes.

Example envelope (literal stringified JSON, use only as illustration):
{
  "schema_version": "1.0.0",
  "event_id": "uuid-1234-abcde",
  "occurred_at": "2026-03-10T15:24:30Z",
  "event_type": "rbac.v2.policy.change",
  "actor": {
    "id": "user-98123",
    "type": "human_user",
    "display_name": "Elena Gomez",
    "origin": "redwood-corp",
    "principal_scope": "org-55"
  },
  "target": [
    {
      "type": "role",
      "id": "role-78",
      "display_name": "Data-Viewer",
      "resource_fingerprint": "sha256:...",
      "external_refs": ["principal:user-98123|resource:dataset-7|perm:read"]
    }
  ],
  "outcome": "success",
  "delta": {
    "type": "kv-diff",
    "entries": [["/roles/role-78/permissions/3", "add", "sha256:null", "sha256:cdef"]]
  },
  "meta": {
    "tenant_id": "org-55",
    "region": "us-west-2"
  }
}

Operational checklist / acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Schema doc checked into confluence + JSON Schema artifact (link to confluence below).
- [ ] Server-side enforcement: writers validate envelope schema_version and required fields; validation library published as npm/go/pip packages.
- [ ] Delta encoder/decoder libs implemented and unit-tested with deterministic fingerprint generation.
- [ ] E2E test that replays a policy migration and produces reconstructable audit trail.
- [ ] Migration plan for existing consumers (console dashboards, external SIEM connectors).

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence proposal: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Unified+Audit+Envelope+Proposal
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9876
- Snapshot store design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Snapshot+Store+Design

Risks and trade-offs:
- Embedding full objects in events increases storage and egress costs; snapshot referencing reduces cost but adds complexity in replay.
- Tokenization allows analytics but complicates investigations across third-party integrations that expect raw identifiers.
- Deterministic fingerprinting requires strict canonicalization; any divergence will break diff verification.

Next steps (short-term):
- Finalize the JSON Schema and publish validation libs (owners: Marco Li, Priya Nambiar).
- Implement writer-side validation in control plane and canary for 2 weeks.
- Kick off migration-engagement for top-5 consumers of audit events (Console, SIEM connector, Dedicated telemetry, Compliance team).
